intent.raw_query: Vancouver food and nature, $1800 solo, 4 days, June 2027, from Seattle

experiences.name: Granville Island Public Market Food Tour

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Vancouver International Airport at 12:00 PM on Flight AC. Take the Canada Line SkyTrain from YVR Airport to downtown Vancouver (approx. 25 min, ~$4 CAD) — the most budget-friendly airport transfer. Check in to Vancouver Harbour Stay and drop off your luggage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Granville Island Public Market Food Tour. Explore the vibrant market, sample local artisan cheeses, fresh Pacific salmon, baked goods, and seasonal produce. Graze your way through the stalls — this doubles as both sightseeing and a budget-friendly lunch. Take the $3.50 Aquabus mini-ferry from downtown for a scenic crossing to Granville Island.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the False Creek seawall back toward downtown to stretch your legs after the flight. Enjoy the waterfront views and get oriented with the city. Wind down with a casual dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and snack on the plane or at the airport — skip the pricey airport restaurants.
meals.lunch: Graze at Granville Island Public Market stalls — try a salmon slider, fresh fruit, and a pastry for under $15 CAD total.
meals.dinner: Noodle Box on Robson Street — generous portions of Asian-inspired noodle bowls for around $14–$16 CAD. Budget-friendly and filling after a travel day.

day_by_day.notes: Canada Line SkyTrain from YVR to Waterfront Station is the cheapest and fastest airport transfer (~$4 CAD with a Compass Card). Pick up a reloadable Compass Card at the airport for all transit during your trip. Granville Island is a short Aquabus ride ($3.50) or a 30-min walk/bike from downtown. Market is open daily 9 AM–7 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Seawall Cycle & Stanley Park Forest Walk. Rent a bike from Spokes Bicycle Rentals near Stanley Park (from ~$8–$10/hr or ~$30/day CAD). Ride the iconic 22km seawall around Stanley Park with stunning views of the North Shore mountains, English Bay, and Burrard Inlet. This is one of Vancouver's best free experiences — just pay for the bike rental.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lock up your bike and venture into Stanley Park's ancient temperate rainforest on foot. Walk the forest trails to Beaver Lake and visit the famous Totem Poles at Brockton Point — both completely free. Return the bike and relax at English Bay Beach, a popular free public beach perfect for a sunny June afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the West End neighbourhood near English Bay for dinner. Browse Denman Street for affordable casual dining options.

meals.breakfast: Grab a bagel and coffee from Tim Hortons or a local cafe near the hotel for under $6 CAD before heading out.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic! Stop at a grocery store (Save-On-Foods or Safeway) before Stanley Park and assemble sandwiches, fruit, and drinks for under $10 CAD. Eat at one of the many picnic tables along the seawall.
meals.dinner: Davie Dosa Company on Davie Street — authentic South Indian dosas and curries for $12–$16 CAD. Vegetarian-friendly and very budget-conscious.

day_by_day.notes: Stanley Park entry is FREE — no admission fee. Bike rentals from Spokes Bicycle Rentals are located right at the park entrance on Georgia Street. June weather in Vancouver is mild (15–20°C) but bring a light jacket as ocean breezes can be cool. The full seawall loop takes 2–3 hours by bike at a leisurely pace.

day_by_day.morning: Lynn Canyon Suspension Bridge & Ecology Centre Hike. Take TransLink buses to Lynn Canyon Park in North Vancouver (use your Compass Card, ~$3.10 CAD each way). This is the FREE alternative to the famous Capilano Suspension Bridge (which costs $65+ CAD). Cross the suspension bridge over the dramatic canyon gorge, visit the free Ecology Centre to learn about old-growth forest ecosystems, and hike through towering Douglas firs and cedars.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking the Twin Falls Trail and 30 Foot Pool Trail within Lynn Canyon Park — both free and spectacular. Bring your swimsuit if the weather is warm as locals swim at the natural pools (check conditions). Head back to Vancouver via bus in the mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Vancouver's historic Chinatown. Walk through the Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden (free to view from outside), browse Pender Street, and soak up the neighbourhood atmosphere before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café Medina on Beatty Street for budget-friendly breakfast — try the oatmeal or toast options for around $8–$10 CAD, or grab groceries from a nearby store for a cheaper self-catered start.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch again from a grocery store or grab snacks before heading to Lynn Canyon — there are no affordable food options in the park itself. Trail mix, sandwiches, and fruit work perfectly.
meals.dinner: Chinatown Night Market & Dim Sum Experience — visit the Chinatown Night Market (free entry, open Fri–Sun evenings in summer) for cheap street food bites, or head to New Town Bakery & Restaurant on Keefer Street for classic dim sum and BBQ dishes for $10–$15 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Lynn Canyon Ecology Centre and Suspension Bridge are 100% FREE — a major budget win compared to Capilano. Take Bus 228 from Lonsdale Quay (reached via SeaBus from Waterfront Station, ~$3.10 CAD) to Lynn Canyon Road. Wear sturdy shoes for hiking. The Chinatown Night Market typically runs Friday–Sunday evenings in summer — check current schedule at vancouverchinatownnightmarket.com.

day_by_day.morning: Revisit or extend your Granville Island experience with a deeper dive into the neighbourhood. Browse the free Net Loft artisan studios and the Kids Market area. Walk along the waterfront and watch local fishermen and float planes. Alternatively, explore Kitsilano Beach (free) — a short bus ride away — for a relaxed morning with mountain views across English Bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Commercial Drive ('The Drive') — Vancouver's most eclectic and budget-friendly neighbourhood. Browse independent shops, street art, and community gardens. This is a great area to pick up affordable local souvenirs, browse vintage stores, and experience authentic Vancouver neighbourhood culture away from the tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening — head back to the waterfront near Vancouver Harbour Stay for a sunset walk along the Coal Harbour seawall. Enjoy the views of the North Shore mountains and float planes landing on the harbour. Pack your bags for departure and reflect on your Vancouver adventure.

meals.breakfast: Grounds for Coffee on Granville Island or grab fresh pastries from the Public Market bakery stalls for $5–$8 CAD — a perfect final morning treat.
meals.lunch: On Commercial Drive, try Havana Restaurant for affordable Cuban-inspired lunch bowls around $14–$16 CAD, or grab a slice from one of the many budget pizza spots on The Drive for under $5 CAD.
meals.dinner: Japadog food cart near Burrard Street or Robson Street — Vancouver's famous Japanese-style hot dogs for $7–$10 CAD. A fun, iconic, and budget-friendly final Vancouver meal. Alternatively, Pho Tan on Kingsway for a large bowl of pho for $12–$14 CAD.

day_by_day.notes: Commercial Drive is easily reached by SkyTrain (Broadway-City Hall station then Bus 99 or walk) or Bus 20 from downtown. If departing early the next morning, consider organizing luggage storage at the hotel to keep your last evening hands-free. The Coal Harbour seawall at sunset is one of Vancouver's most beautiful free experiences — don't miss it on a clear June evening.

trip_options.title: Classic Vancouver Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Vancouver International Airport at 12:00 PM on Flight AC. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Canada Line SkyTrain directly from YVR to downtown Vancouver (~25 min, ~$10 CAD). Check in to Vancouver Harbour Stay and freshen up. Take a leisurely stroll along the waterfront near Canada Place to get your bearings and soak in the harbour views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Granville Island Public Market Food Tour: Head to Granville Island via a short taxi or False Creek ferry (~$5 CAD, 10 min). Explore the vibrant Public Market, sampling local artisan cheeses, fresh Pacific salmon, charcuterie, baked goods, and regional preserves. Browse the artisan stalls and enjoy the lively atmosphere. Allow 2–3 hours to wander at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the downtown core and explore Yaletown neighbourhood on foot. Enjoy a casual dinner at one of Yaletown's mid-range restaurants before an early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at the airport or on arrival — Tim Hortons or Waves Coffee near YVR (~$8–12 CAD)
meals.lunch: Graze the stalls at Granville Island Public Market — build your own spread from the vendors: smoked salmon, artisan bread, local cheese, and fresh fruit (~$20–28 CAD)
meals.dinner: Yaletown Brewing Company — classic Canadian pub fare with locally brewed craft beers in a relaxed setting (~$25–40 CAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the noon arrival. The False Creek ferry from downtown to Granville Island is a scenic and fun way to cross — look for the Aquabus or False Creek Ferries near the convention centre waterfront. Pack comfortable walking shoes. June in Vancouver is mild (16–22°C) but keep a light jacket handy in case of coastal breezes.

day_by_day.morning: Seawall Cycle & Stanley Park Forest Walk: Start the day early with a bike rental near Coal Harbour (~$8–12 CAD/hour, or ~$35–45 CAD for a half-day from Spokes Bicycle Rentals near Stanley Park entrance). Ride the iconic 22km seawall loop around Stanley Park with stunning views of the North Shore mountains, Lions Gate Bridge, and English Bay. Take your time — the full loop takes about 1.5–2 hours of leisurely cycling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lock up or return the bikes and venture into Stanley Park's ancient temperate rainforest on foot. Walk the forest trails to visit the famous totem poles at Brockton Point, Beaver Lake, and the hollow tree. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the forest interior before heading back toward downtown.
day_by_day.evening: Chinatown Night Market & Dim Sum Experience: Head to Vancouver's historic Chinatown (a short 15-min taxi or bus ride from downtown). Browse the vibrant night market stalls for street food snacks, local crafts, and cultural finds. Explore the Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden (~$14 CAD admission) if open in the evening, or simply stroll Pender and Keefer Streets to soak up the atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Catch a quick breakfast near the hotel before heading out — Café Medina on Richards Street is a Vancouver favourite for brunch with Belgian waffles and lavender lattes (~$18–25 CAD)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch at Second Beach or English Bay within Stanley Park — grab supplies from a park concession stand or bring snacks from a nearby grocery store (~$12–18 CAD)
meals.dinner: Chinatown dining — New Town Bakery & Restaurant for BBQ pork buns and congee, or Phnom Penh for iconic Vietnamese-Cambodian dishes beloved by locals (~$18–28 CAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Stanley Park seawall is best enjoyed in the morning before crowds build up. Bike rentals are plentiful near the Georgia Street park entrance. The seawall is well-signed and paved — suitable for all fitness levels. For Chinatown, the night market typically runs Thursday–Sunday evenings in summer; if visiting on a Tuesday, focus on the restaurant scene and garden instead. Confirm Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Garden hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Squamish Sea-to-Sky Gondola Day Trip: Depart the hotel by 8:00 AM for the scenic 1-hour drive up the Sea-to-Sky Highway (Hwy 99) toward Squamish. Rent a car for the day (~$60–80 CAD) or book a shuttle/tour from Vancouver. Ride the Sea-to-Sky Gondola (~$59 CAD adults) to the summit at 885m elevation for breathtaking panoramic views of Howe Sound, glaciers, and coastal peaks. Walk the summit trails including the Sky Pilot Suspension Bridge and Chief Overlook trail (allow 2–3 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend via gondola and explore the base area. Drive back along the Sea-to-Sky Highway at a leisurely pace, stopping at Shannon Falls Provincial Park (~10 min from the gondola base) to see BC's third-highest waterfall — a short 500m walk from the parking area. Return to Vancouver by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Chef's Table Dinner: Treat yourself to the recommended chef's table or tasting menu dinner experience in Vancouver as a highlight evening. Head to the Gastown neighbourhood for dinner at a celebrated local restaurant featuring Pacific Northwest cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Early departure — grab coffee and a breakfast sandwich to go from a downtown café or 7-Eleven before hitting the road (~$8–12 CAD)
meals.lunch: Summit Café at the Sea-to-Sky Gondola top station — enjoy a hot meal with incredible mountain views (burgers, soups, sandwiches; ~$18–26 CAD per person)
meals.dinner: Gastown splurge — L'Abattoir or Wildebeest for inventive Pacific Northwest cuisine with locally sourced ingredients (~$50–70 CAD per person with drinks — a worthwhile mid-trip treat)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Sea-to-Sky Gondola tickets online in advance to guarantee entry, especially in peak June season. The drive up Hwy 99 is one of Canada's most scenic — allow extra time for photo stops at Horseshoe Bay and Britannia Beach. If you prefer not to rent a car, Epic Rides or Landsea Tours offer guided day trips from Vancouver that include gondola access. Wear layers at the summit — temperatures can be 5–8°C cooler than Vancouver even in June.

day_by_day.morning: Lynn Canyon Suspension Bridge & Ecology Centre Hike: Take a taxi or TransLink bus to Lynn Canyon Park in North Vancouver (~35–45 min from downtown). This is a wonderful free alternative to the famous Capilano Suspension Bridge. Cross the free suspension bridge over a dramatic gorge with rushing turquoise water below, then hike through old-growth Douglas fir and cedar forest. Visit the Lynn Canyon Ecology Centre (free admission) to learn about the temperate rainforest ecosystem. Allow 2.5–3 hours for the hike and exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Vancouver and spend the afternoon in the Kitsilano neighbourhood. Browse the boutiques and bookshops along 4th Avenue, visit the Vancouver Maritime Museum (~$15 CAD) or simply relax at Kitsilano Beach with views of the North Shore mountains. Pick up any last-minute souvenirs at local shops.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Vancouver — return to the waterfront near your hotel for a sunset walk along the Coal Harbour seawall. Enjoy a farewell dinner in the West End neighbourhood, then pack and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Café Calabria or Breka Bakery & Café near downtown for a proper sit-down breakfast of eggs, toast, and fresh-pressed juice (~$14–20 CAD)
meals.lunch: Grab lunch in Kitsilano — The Naam (Vancouver's legendary vegetarian restaurant, open since 1968) for hearty veggie burgers, soups, and smoothies (~$16–24 CAD)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Cardero's Restaurant on Coal Harbour — fresh Pacific seafood and West Coast cuisine with stunning harbour and mountain views as a perfect send-off (~$40–55 CAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Lynn Canyon is free to enter — a great budget-friendly nature experience for the final morning. Wear sturdy shoes as some trails can be uneven and damp. The park has multiple trail loops ranging from 30 minutes to 2+ hours; the Twin Falls trail is highly recommended for waterfall views. TransLink bus route 228 from Lonsdale Quay (reached via SeaBus from Waterfront Station) serves the park. Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your departure flight is in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Hotel Check-In: Flight AC lands at 12:00 PM. Transfer by private car service to Vancouver Harbour Stay. Settle into your luxury suite, freshen up, and take in the stunning harbour views from your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: Granville Island Public Market Food Tour: After settling in, head to the iconic Granville Island Public Market for an immersive guided food tour. Sample artisan cheeses, fresh Pacific salmon, hand-crafted charcuterie, locally baked breads, and seasonal preserves from award-winning vendors. Stroll the waterfront boardwalk afterward and browse the artisan studios.
day_by_day.evening: Waterfront Fine Dining & Harbour Sunset: Enjoy a leisurely evening at a world-class waterfront restaurant near the harbour. Savour a multi-course tasting menu featuring BC spot prawns, sablefish, and locally foraged ingredients paired with premium BC VQA wines.

meals.breakfast: N/A – mid-day arrival; grab a light snack at the airport or on board
meals.lunch: Granville Island Market grazing: artisan cheese boards, smoked salmon, fresh-baked sourdough, and local charcuterie from market vendors
meals.dinner: Blue Water Cafe + Raw Bar (Yaletown) – celebrated for its ultra-fresh Pacific seafood and an exceptional BC wine list; reserve the chef's table for a premium experience

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private luxury transfer from Vancouver International Airport (YVR) to the hotel. Contact the hotel concierge in advance to pre-stock the room with a welcome amenity – local BC wines, artisan chocolates, and fresh flowers. Book the Granville Island Food Tour guide ahead of time for a private session.

day_by_day.morning: Seawall Cycle & Stanley Park Forest Walk: Begin the day with a premium bike rental (or private e-bike guided tour) along the iconic 22 km seawall encircling Stanley Park. Enjoy sweeping views of the North Shore mountains, Lions Gate Bridge, and English Bay. Transition from the seawall into Stanley Park's ancient temperate rainforest trails – walk among towering Douglas firs and red cedars, visit the totem poles at Brockton Point, and breathe in the old-growth atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Chinatown Exploration & Dim Sum Experience: After the morning in nature, head to Vancouver's historic Chinatown – one of the largest in North America. Enjoy a premium dim sum lunch at a top-rated establishment. Explore the Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden (private guided tour available), a UNESCO-recognized gem of Ming Dynasty architecture and tranquil landscaping.
day_by_day.evening: Chinatown Night Market & Cocktail Bar: Return to Chinatown as the evening energy builds. Explore the vibrant Night Market stalls for street food bites – scallion pancakes, BBQ skewers, and mango shaved ice. Cap the night at a sophisticated cocktail bar in Gastown, just steps away, featuring BC craft spirits and locally inspired cocktails.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at Vancouver Harbour Stay – order the full à la carte spread with Dungeness crab eggs benedict, smoked BC salmon, and freshly squeezed juice
meals.lunch: Kirin Restaurant (Chinatown/City Square) – refined Cantonese dim sum with premium options including har gow, XO scallop dumplings, and Peking duck
meals.dinner: Mott 32 Vancouver – award-winning modern Chinese cuisine in a stunning heritage bank building; signature Applewood roasted Peking duck and premium seafood dishes

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book a private e-bike guide for the Stanley Park seawall for the most seamless and informative experience. Request a private guided tour of Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden through the hotel concierge. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the forest trail section. Gastown and Chinatown are walkable from each other – ideal for an evening stroll.

day_by_day.morning: Squamish Sea-to-Sky Gondola Summit Experience: Depart early by private luxury vehicle along the dramatic Sea-to-Sky Highway (Highway 99) to Squamish, approximately one hour from Vancouver. Ascend the Sea-to-Sky Gondola to the summit at 885 metres for breathtaking panoramic views of Howe Sound, glaciers, and ancient coastal peaks. Walk the Sky Pilot Suspension Bridge and explore the summit trail network through subalpine forest and wildflower meadows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Chef's Table Lunch at the Summit & Shannon Falls Detour: Enjoy the exclusive Chef's Table experience at the gondola's Summit Lodge – a curated multi-course menu showcasing BC ingredients with a backdrop of Howe Sound. On the return drive, stop at Shannon Falls Provincial Park (BC's third-highest waterfall) for a short, awe-inspiring walk to the base of the 335-metre cascade.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury Spa Evening at the Hotel: Return to Vancouver Harbour Stay and indulge in an in-hotel or nearby luxury spa treatment – a deep-tissue massage, Pacific seaweed wrap, or couples' hydrotherapy ritual. Dine at a celebrated Yaletown or Coal Harbour restaurant for an intimate, refined dinner.

meals.breakfast: Light in-hotel breakfast before departure – fresh pastries, seasonal fruit, and single-origin pour-over coffee to fuel the morning drive
meals.lunch: Chef's Table at Sea-to-Sky Gondola Summit Lodge – multi-course locally sourced BC menu with panoramic Howe Sound views; reserve well in advance
meals.dinner: Hawksworth Restaurant (Downtown Vancouver) – one of Canada's most acclaimed fine-dining restaurants; seasonal tasting menu with optional premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Depart by 8:30 AM to arrive at the gondola before peak crowds and maximize summit time. Book the Chef's Table at the Summit Lodge weeks in advance as it fills quickly. Private car hire for the Sea-to-Sky drive is strongly recommended for flexibility and comfort. Confirm spa reservations at the hotel before the day begins.

day_by_day.morning: Lynn Canyon Suspension Bridge & Ecology Centre Hike: Head to Lynn Canyon Park in North Vancouver by private car (approximately 25 minutes from the hotel). Hike through stunning old-growth forest, cross the free suspension bridge dramatically suspended over the canyon gorge, and explore the Lynn Canyon Ecology Centre for fascinating insights into the coastal rainforest ecosystem. Continue on the Baden-Powell or Twin Falls trail for a deeper immersion into the wilderness.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lonsdale Quay Market & North Shore Exploration: Descend to the waterfront and explore the Lonsdale Quay Public Market – a more intimate, local alternative to Granville Island. Browse artisan food stalls, BC craft beer vendors, and specialty shops. Take the scenic SeaBus back across Burrard Inlet to Downtown Vancouver – a 12-minute harbour crossing with spectacular skyline views – perfect for a final afternoon in the city.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Luxury Dinner & Harbour Views: Celebrate your final evening in Vancouver with a spectacular farewell dinner at one of the city's premier fine-dining establishments overlooking Coal Harbour or the waterfront. Savour a curated menu of the best Pacific Northwest cuisine – wild BC salmon, Vancouver Island scallops, truffle-infused risotto – paired with a sommelier-selected wine flight. Stroll the Coal Harbour seawall at dusk for a magical last memory of the city.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel champagne breakfast – smoked salmon eggs royale, fresh berry parfait, and a Bloody Caesar (Canada's iconic cocktail) to start the final day in style
meals.lunch: Lonsdale Quay Market, North Vancouver – graze on artisan charcuterie, Pacific oysters on the half shell, BC craft ales, and freshly made sushi rolls from premium market vendors
meals.dinner: Ancora Waterfront Dining & Patio (Coal Harbour) – stunning waterfront setting with Peruvian-Japanese influenced Pacific seafood; signature ceviche, miso-glazed sablefish, and a world-class pisco sour to close the trip

day_by_day.notes: Lynn Canyon Park is free to enter – a wonderful contrast to the commercial Capilano Suspension Bridge nearby, and equally spectacular. Wear sturdy hiking shoes with grip for the canyon trails. The SeaBus from Lonsdale Quay to Waterfront Station runs every 15–30 minutes and offers one of the best free views of the Vancouver skyline. Arrange a private car transfer to YVR the following morning through the hotel concierge.
